solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Excuse for Scotch sounding anything but genuine

indicators.note: sounding asks for a word that is spoken like the phrase that follows, not spelt like it

parts.note: something anything but genuine is fake

explanation.surface: A poor excuse offered for a bottle of Scotch whisky that sounds anything but genuine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for Scotch' marks the definition as a Scots word, not whisky: FAIK is Scots for to excuse or let off.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots dialect, faik is a verb meaning to excuse or let someone off, recorded in Chambers.

clue.text: Bosom pal sailors' bar employs having a chinwag inside (12, two words)

parts.note: a fid is a tapered bar or pin used by sailors for rope work

indicators.note: having something inside means one word holds the other within it
inside confirms the chat sits within the other word

parts.note: employs means uses
a chinwag is a chat

explanation.surface: Two old sailor friends gossiping in the bar where they drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Fidus Achates is 'faithful Achates', loyal companion of Aeneas in Virgil, hence any devoted friend.
explanation.definitionFit: Achates was the faithful companion of Aeneas in the Aeneid, so his Latin epithet names a loyal intimate friend.

clue.text: Herb sauce mostly sloshed around 'hare' of a kind

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped
around means the jumbled letters enclose another word
sloshed means drunk, so the letters reel into a new order

parts.note: sauce with its last letter removed
the mara is a long-legged Patagonian rodent often called a hare

explanation.surface: A cook drunkenly sloshing sauce around a jugged hare.
explanation.walkthrough: The quotes round 'hare' flag that the animal is not a true hare: the mara is a cavy.
explanation.definitionFit: Amaracus is an old name for marjoram, an aromatic culinary herb.

clue.text: Pairs changing places catch salmon

indicators.note: the two-letter halves of the word swap round, front pair to the back

parts.note: to catch is to take

explanation.surface: Anglers taking turns in pairs to land a salmon.
explanation.definitionFit: The keta is the chum salmon of the North Pacific, a species name used in Chambers.

clue.text: Doctor with a c-cure unusually introduced for health (8, two words)

indicators.note: introduced means put inside another word

parts.note: GP is a general practitioner, a family doctor

indicators.note: unusually means the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: the letters taken as written, hyphen ignored

explanation.surface: A doctor with a stammered cure brought in for someone's health.
explanation.walkthrough: 'health' is the toast, as in drinking someone's health, not physical wellbeing.
explanation.definitionFit: A grace cup is a cup passed round after grace for a final toast, so it is a health drunk at table.

clue.text: Arrives in old-style check when climbing shrubby US plateaux

indicators.note: in places one word inside the other
in a down clue climbing means read from bottom to top

parts.note: sneb is an obsolete form of snub, to check or rebuke
arr. is the timetable abbreviation for arrives

explanation.surface: Someone arrives at an old-fashioned checkpoint while climbing American uplands.
explanation.walkthrough: The old form SNEB, turned upward, wraps round the timetable abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: In North America barrens are tracts of poor land with scrubby growth, often on high plateaux.

clue.text: Most radios (not all) will need regular tuning

definitions.note: a descriptive definition: the thing that will need regular tuning

indicators.note: not all of the words are used, only a run of letters inside them

parts.note: the letters run across the join of the two words

explanation.surface: A complaint that most radio sets need constant retuning.
explanation.walkthrough: Tuning suggests radio stations; the answer is a violin, which must be tuned by ear.
explanation.definitionFit: A Strad, a Stradivarius violin, must be tuned before playing like any string instrument.

clue.text: Cheers dance offering in certain bars

parts.note: ta is an informal British thank-you, like cheers
a pas is a step or dance in ballet

explanation.surface: Raising a toast to a dance being performed in a bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bars' looks like music, given the dance, but means Spanish bars.
explanation.definitionFit: Tapas are small savoury dishes served with drinks in Spanish bars.

clue.text: Bottle, second imbibed, making one up-beat

indicators.note: something imbibed is drunk down, so it ends up inside

parts.note: Cockney rhyming slang: bottle and glass gives arse, and Aristotle gives aris, both for bottom; bottle is also courage
s is the abbreviation for second

explanation.surface: A bottle with a quick drink taken in that puts one in an upbeat mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Aris is rhyming-slang for the backside, and so, like bottle, it stands for the same.
explanation.definitionFit: In music arsis is the unaccented beat or part of a bar, the upbeat.

clue.text: Heretics in past are converted

indicators.note: converted means changed into another form

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Heretics who have since been converted to orthodoxy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'converted' fits the religious picture but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Patarines were an eleventh-century Milanese reform movement later used as a name for Cathar and other heretical sects.

clue.text: Make good muscle with extremes of effort

parts.note: ab is short for an abdominal muscle

indicators.note: extremes are the two ends, so only the first and last letters are kept

parts.note: first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Building muscle with a lot of hard effort.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Make good' is the old sense of backing up or maintaining a claim.
explanation.definitionFit: To abet once meant to maintain or support, and making good a claim is supporting it.

clue.text: Dodder maybe, having left little in rum, tiny dimension

indicators.note: in puts one letter inside the other word

parts.note: rum is British slang for strange
left in little, that is abbreviated, form
wee is Scots for tiny
D stands for dimension, as in 3D

explanation.surface: A tiny measure of rum left over in a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'little' tells you to cut left to its abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Dodder is a parasitic twining plant that chokes its hosts, an example of a strangleweed.

clue.text: One in Rome trip reread e.g. Caesar

indicators.note: in places one item inside a group of letters
reread suggests the letters are read again in a different order

parts.note: the letters taken as written
a means one

explanation.surface: A tourist on a Roman holiday rereading about Julius Caesar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One in Rome' looks like a Roman numeral I, but one is the article, placed among the trip's letters before the shuffle.
explanation.definitionFit: Imperator was the Roman title of a victorious commander, later of the emperor, which Caesar bore.

clue.text: Office mad on army regulation

parts.note: daft means mad
AR is the abbreviation for Army Regulation

explanation.surface: A complaint that the office has gone mad on army-style rules.
explanation.walkthrough: DAFTAR is an Anglo-Indian word, from Persian.
explanation.definitionFit: In India a daftar is an office or a record-keeping bureau, a word listed in Chambers.

clue.text: Oven turkey maybe without a stuffing put in a roll

indicators.note: without means the item named is left out
stuffing tells you the removed letter comes from the middle of the word

parts.note: a roaster is a bird reared for the oven, a turkey for instance
taken as written

explanation.surface: An oven-ready turkey, unstuffed, put into a bread roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roll' looks like bread but means a list of names.
explanation.definitionFit: As a verb, roster means to enter someone on a duty list or roll.

clue.text: Act of following prize money consumes united amateur northern clubs

indicators.note: one thing consumes another by taking it inside

parts.note: a purse is the money put up as a prize
U is the abbreviation for united
A is the abbreviation for amateur
N is the abbreviation for northern
C is the card abbreviation for clubs

explanation.surface: Prize money swallowed up by a group of united amateur football clubs in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: The sporting surface hides four single-letter abbreviations taken into the purse.
explanation.definitionFit: Pursuance is the carrying out or following through of a plan or course, a pursuit.

clue.text: Major group within phylum, feline one, queen protected

indicators.note: something protected is surrounded and shielded by another

parts.note: a cat is a feline
a rani is an Indian queen
a means one

explanation.surface: A zoologist's note on a cat in a phylum, a protected queen among them.
explanation.walkthrough: The rani sits inside the cat; the article follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Craniata, animals with skulls, is a major subdivision of the phylum Chordata.

clue.text: To the French occupying old service this is lightly fried

indicators.note: occupying means sitting within something

parts.note: steed is an obsolete spelling of stead, meaning service or use
au is French for to the

explanation.surface: A French chef's old method of service, lightly frying the food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stand in good stead' keeps the old sense of service; Chambers gives the obsolete spelling.
explanation.definitionFit: Sauteed food is cooked quickly in a little hot fat, which is frying lightly.

clue.text: German gent holds bag, bursting, with yen for wild cherry

indicators.note: holds means encloses another word

parts.note: Herr is the German for Mr or gentleman

indicators.note: something bursting breaks apart, so its letters scatter

parts.note: taken as written
Y is the abbreviation for the yen

explanation.surface: A German man with a bursting bag and a craving for wild cherries.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yen' looks like a longing but is the Japanese currency.
explanation.definitionFit: Hagberry is a northern name for the bird cherry, a wild cherry tree.

clue.text: Shakespeare's complex, in brief moment encapsulating central character in machination

indicators.note: encapsulating means enclosing as if in a capsule

parts.note: in a trice, a brief moment, with the article left out

indicators.note: the central character of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the sixth of its eleven letters

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare scholar unpicking a complex plot in a brief moment.
explanation.walkthrough: INTRINCE is a Shakespearean coinage, used in King Lear.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare uses intrince to mean intricate or tangled, which is what complex means.

clue.text: Well-ordered pupils bloom without us

indicators.note: without means the following letters are taken away

parts.note: a crocus is a spring flower
taken as written

explanation.surface: Tidy schoolchildren in bloom, without the rest of us.
explanation.walkthrough: A crocodile, short form croc, is a British school word for children walking in a line in pairs.
explanation.definitionFit: A crocodile of schoolchildren walks in orderly pairs, and croc is its informal clipping.

clue.text: Treatment resented by stewardesses from old man on flight?

parts.note: pa is father, the old man
a wing is what makes flight possible; on the wing means in flight

explanation.surface: Cabin crew annoyed by a groping elderly passenger on an aeroplane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'old man' reads as a passenger but is the family word for father.
explanation.definitionFit: Pawing is unwanted touching or groping, which cabin staff rightly resent.

clue.text: Sailor following chart of what he walks on?

indicators.note: following means placed after the other part

parts.note: a plan is a chart or diagram
tar is an old word for a sailor

explanation.surface: A sailor consulting a chart of the deck he walks on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'he' seems to be the sailor, but the definition is about anyone's feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Plantar means relating to the sole of the foot, the part a person walks on.

clue.text: Tree creature as a normal rule avoiding tom repeatedly

indicators.note: repeatedly means the remaining piece is set down twice in a row
avoiding means leaving out the item named

parts.note: custom is what is normally done, used adjectivally
taken as written

explanation.surface: A tree-dwelling animal that normally keeps away from the tomcat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tom' looks like a male cat chasing the creature; it is only three letters to strip.
explanation.definitionFit: The cuscus is a tree-dwelling marsupial of New Guinea and northern Australia.

clue.text: Old noble affecting entry without much of entourage

indicators.note: the surrounding letters, the entourage, are mostly stripped away to leave a core

parts.note: the last letter of the first word joined to the start of the second

explanation.surface: An old aristocrat making an affected entrance with barely any retinue.
explanation.walkthrough: GENT here is the obsolete adjective meaning noble or gentle, not the man.
explanation.definitionFit: Gent was an old adjective, from French, meaning noble, graceful or well-born.

clue.text: Fiddle a company's underwritten offering anti-venom stuff

indicators.note: in a down clue written underneath means the next part follows below

parts.note: the gu or gue was a kind of fiddle once played in Shetland
taken as written
Co is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: A fraudulent company underwriting a dubious anti-venom remedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' suggests fraud, which suits the surface, but is the old Shetland violin.
explanation.definitionFit: Guaco is a tropical American climbing plant whose juice was used as a remedy for snakebite.

clue.text: See old drummer err, beat being off key

indicators.note: playing off key means wrong, so the letters come out wrongly ordered

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Watching a drummer go wrong and play his beat off key.
explanation.walkthrough: TABRERE is Spenser's spelling of taborer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabrere in Spenser is a taborer, one who plays the tabor, a small drum.

clue.text: Quantity added in US chemistry lab, more precise by the sound of it

definitions.text: Quantity added in US chemistry lab

indicators.note: by the sound of it means the word is judged by how it is spoken

parts.note: tighter means stricter or more exact, said without the r in non-rhotic speech

explanation.surface: An American chemist adding a carefully measured amount for more precision.
explanation.walkthrough: TITER is the American spelling of titre; in British speech it sounds like the comparative of tight.
explanation.definitionFit: A titre is the measured volume of a solution needed to reach the end point in a titration.

clue.text: A membrane that is surrounding number of stemless plants

indicators.note: surrounding means enclosing another item

parts.note: taken as written
a caul is a membrane, as round a newborn's head
i.e. is Latin id est, that is
n stands for a number in maths

explanation.surface: A botanist describing a membrane surrounding a number of stemless plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'number of' reads as a quantity but N stands for number and 'of' starts the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Acauline is a botanical adjective meaning having no visible stem, from Greek a- without and Latin caulis, stem.

clue.text: Billy (from Boston?) getting very uplifted in church

indicators.note: in places one word inside another

parts.note: ch is the abbreviation for church

indicators.note: uplifted in a down clue means read upwards

parts.note: so means very

explanation.surface: A man called Billy from Boston being very spiritually uplifted at church.
explanation.walkthrough: A billy, or billy club, is the American word for a policeman's truncheon, hence 'from Boston'.
explanation.definitionFit: A cosh is a short heavy bludgeon, what Americans call a billy club.

clue.text: Christian, one in love going heavenward?

indicators.note: going heavenward in a down clue means read upwards
in places one word inside another

parts.note: nix means nothing, and love is nothing in tennis
a means one

explanation.surface: A Christian in love rising to heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: X stands for Christ, from the Greek chi, so XIAN is the old abbreviation of Christian.
explanation.definitionFit: Xian is a written short form of Christian, X being the Greek initial of Christ.

clue.text: Granny laid into small child, fulminating

indicators.note: laid into means set inside another word

parts.note: a tot is a small child
nan is a British word for grandmother

explanation.surface: A grandmother laying into a toddler and fuming at it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'laid into' reads as scolding, which suits fulminating, but is the insertion signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Tonant means thundering, from Latin tonare, and fulminating is thundering too.

clue.text: Those musketeers, and fourth in group, go around

definitions.note: the answer is an adjective; the definition describes the trio as three in one

indicators.note: around means one word encloses the other

parts.note: trine is an old word meaning to go

indicators.note: fourth in means take the fourth letter of the next word

parts.note: fourth letter of the word

explanation.surface: The Three Musketeers and a fourth member gathering round.
explanation.walkthrough: The musketeers swore 'all for one', three acting as one; d'Artagnan made the fourth.
explanation.definitionFit: Triune means three in one, as the musketeers acted with a single will.

clue.text: Eviction, malignancy mostly involving tragic monarch

indicators.note: mostly means all but the final letter
involving means wrapping around something

parts.note: cancer, a malignancy, without its last letter
King Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king

explanation.surface: A deadly eviction like that suffered by Lear, turned out by his daughters.
explanation.walkthrough: The Highland Clearances are the classic case of mass eviction.
explanation.definitionFit: Clearance is the removal of people from land or buildings, as in the Highland Clearances.

clue.text: Hell holes, chaotic

indicators.note: chaotic means in disorder, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: Hell holes in a state of chaos.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheol is the Hebrew underworld, the abode of the dead, often rendered as hell.

clue.text: How some treat dough, we hear, causing penury

indicators.note: we hear means the word is judged by its spoken form

parts.note: bakers work dough by kneading it

explanation.surface: Mishandling the money, dough, causing poverty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dough' is slang for money, which feeds the poverty picture; here it is bread dough.
explanation.definitionFit: Need in the sense of want or poverty is a synonym for penury.
